summary: This version of the playlist app puts whole Song objects into a PriorityQueue instead of plain numbers or strings, using a comparator on each song's energy level so the queue always hands back the most energetic song first. A poll() loop drains the queue, printing songs in descending order of energy.

lines.text: PriorityQueue is the queue that keeps its elements ordered by priority rather than by arrival time, so the head is always the "most important" element.
Declaring the queue as PriorityQueue<Song> means it stores real domain objects, so nothing is lost the way it would be if you only queued titles or energy numbers.
A Song has no natural ordering, so the queue is given a comparator that reads each song's energy level; .reversed() flips the usual smallest-first rule into highest-energy-first.
addAll copies every song from the existing list in one call, and the queue quietly arranges them internally according to the comparator as they go in.
Because poll() removes elements, checking isEmpty() each time round is how you drain the queue exactly once per song.

lines.code: Song nextSong = energyQueue.poll(); // highest energy first
lines.text: poll() removes and returns the head of the queue, which under this comparator is always the highest-energy song still waiting.
Concatenating the object into a string calls the Song class's toString method, which is why a whole song's details appear instead of a memory address.
